note: Hedged and unsourceable as written. Better repair: cite the documented 玉子の天婦羅 on the lunch don menu (https://www.zameshi.com/entry/2020/11/06/190000) as the concrete egg presence, instead of speculating about the batter.

quote: Tentsuyu built on dashi that is normally bonito (fish) stock.
found: No source names the tentsuyu dashi. Worth noting a stronger, documented vegan obstacle instead: every lunch set on this menu ships with 味噌汁 (天婦羅ランチ, 天婦羅膳, 上天婦羅膳, 大海老天丼, かき揚げ丼 all list 「味噌汁・香の物」), whose dashi is likewise undocumented.
note: Category-level assumption, no venue evidence. If kept, pair it with the sourced fact that every set includes miso soup — that is the real per-visit exposure.

quote: No published allergen program or gluten-free menu found; staff should be asked directly.
found: Confirmed silence across all four: the official gorp page has five こだわり entries and no allergen text; Gnavi has zero hits for アレル; Tabelog 店舗情報 lists 席数17/全席禁煙/カウンター席あり and no allergen field.
method: official JSON + Gnavi + s.tabelog (iPhone UA) + blog
note: UNCITED but verified absence — anchor to https://tempura-abe-ginza.gorp.jp/ and https://tabelog.com/tokyo/A1301/A130101/13092132/.

quote: English-speaking staff available for questions.
found: Official site 店舗情報 payload, verbatim: "foreign_lang":{"menu":null,"staff":"英語"} — English-speaking staff, but NO English menu.
method: 1 plain fetch, JSON field read directly
note: UNCITED but exactly confirmed — cite https://tempura-abe-ginza.gorp.jp/. Add the other half the same field states: there is no foreign-language menu, so a written Japanese celiac card matters more, not less.

quote: Rock salt (岩塩) offered alongside tentsuyu, letting a diner skip the wheat-soy dipping sauce (the batter still contains wheat).
found: The salts are SEA salts, not rock salt. Ginza-meshi blog: 「テーブルには、2種類の塩が置かれていて自由に使える。左が「梅塩」、右が「フランス産の海の塩」。」 Tabelog reviewers: 「塩2種（藻塩と赤紫蘇梅塩⁈）」 and 「天つゆ、大根おろし、塩二種、レモンが用意されています」. 岩塩 returns zero hits on the official site, on Gnavi, on Tabelog and across a Yahoo Japan search of this shop.
method: blog fetch + mobile-host Tabelog + Yahoo Japan exact search for 天ぷら 阿部 銀座本店 岩塩
note: The substance survives, the detail is invented: two table salts DO let a diner skip the tentsuyu, but they are 梅塩 and フランス産の海の塩 (some reviewers read them as 藻塩/赤紫蘇梅塩), never 岩塩. Rewrite as "two table salts (plum salt and French sea salt)" and cite https://www.zameshi.com/entry/2020/11/06/190000.

quote: A vegetable/vegetarian tempura course exists as a starting point for plant-based diners to negotiate from.
found: Official おすすめ menu, first item: 「季節を感じる旬の厳選野菜全十一品を堪能『阿部特製ベジタリアンコース』 5500円（税込）/ 1名様」 — also carried on Gnavi.
note: UNCITED but better than the claim suggests — this is a named, priced, 11-course house vegetarian menu, not something to "negotiate from". Cite https://tempura-abe-ginza.gorp.jp/. Still vegetarian, not vegan: tentsuyu dashi, the accompanying 味噌汁 and the house 玉子の天婦羅 are all unresolved.

OPEN AND TRADING — Tabelog https://tabelog.com/tokyo/A1301/A130101/13092132/ carries no 閉店 banner, the official page shows current hours (lunch 11:30, dinner 17:00-21:00, closed only 大晦日・元旦) and Gnavi is running live reservations. gf "no" is correct and needs no argument. vegan "ask" is right: a named 『阿部特製ベジタリアンコース』(11 seasonal vegetable items, 5,500 yen) exists, but it is vegetarian, and the tentsuyu dashi, the miso soup on every set and the house 玉子の天婦羅 are unresolved — not enough for "options". All 10 claims were uncited; 6 are now evidenced from the official site / Tabelog / the Ginza-meshi blog, 3 are cuisine-level assumptions with no venue evidence (batter flour, batter egg, bonito tentsuyu), and 1 is factually wrong: there is no 岩塩 here — the table salts are 梅塩 and フランス産の海の塩.
